ga.name: Georgia
ga.tagline: One of the most aggressive HEAR/HOMES rollouts in the nation
notes: Launched both HOMES and HEAR early via approved-contractor pilot
Low-income households (≤80% AMI) get 100% of project costs covered
Moderate-income (80–150% AMI) get 50% coverage
Whole-home projects ≥35% savings can reach up to $16k in HOMES rebates
Georgia Power and EMCs offer additional heat pump rebates
Strong contractor network already certified and onboarded

nc.name: North Carolina
nc.tagline: Aggressive early adopter with streamlined contractor onboarding
notes: One of the first states to launch full HEAR program
Duke Energy and other utilities provide stacking rebates
Simplified income verification for qualified households
Strong focus on rural electrification and manufactured housing
Contractor training programs widely available

me.name: Maine
me.tagline: Community-focused electrification with strong utility partnerships
notes: Efficiency Maine Trust coordinates HEAR/HOMES delivery
Additional state weatherization funds for comprehensive retrofits
Cold-climate heat pump focus (proven down to -15°F)
Strong emphasis on oil-to-heat-pump conversions
Income-qualified households can combine HEAR + weatherization assistance

nm.name: New Mexico
nm.tagline: Equity-centered program with enhanced low-income benefits
notes: Strong tribal and rural outreach programs
PNM and other utilities offer heat pump rebates that stack with HEAR
Low-income households prioritized with dedicated contractor network
Mobile home and manufactured housing upgrades eligible
Spanish-language application support widely available

ny.name: New York
ny.tagline: Nation's most comprehensive home energy program with aggressive electrification goals
notes: NYSERDA coordinates stacking of federal HEAR + state EmPower/Clean Heat programs
ConEd and other utility territories offer additional rebates
Low-income households can access up to $24k+ in combined incentives
Mandatory contractor certification and quality assurance programs
Whole-home energy assessments required for HOMES
Strong focus on multifamily and affordable housing

ca.name: California
ca.tagline: Leading the nation in clean energy incentives and building electrification
notes: TECH Clean California provides enhanced heat pump rebates beyond federal caps
Bay Area and SoCal utilities (PG&E, SCE, SoCalGas) offer extensive stacking rebates
Building Performance Institute (BPI) certification widely available
Equity segments prioritized: low-income, disadvantaged communities (DACs)
Whole-home electrification pathways supported with comprehensive rebates
Additional local incentives from air quality districts (BAAQMD, SCAQMD)

co.name: Colorado
co.tagline: Strong utility coordination with Xcel Energy and municipal partnerships
notes: Xcel Energy offers some of the highest utility heat pump rebates in the nation
Income-qualified customers can combine HEAR + utility + weatherization funds
Strong focus on high-altitude and cold-climate heat pump technologies
Municipal utilities (Fort Collins, Colorado Springs) have additional programs
Whole-home energy coaching available through Energy Smart Colorado

az.name: Arizona
az.tagline: Utility-driven pilot with SRP and APS partnerships
notes: SRP (Salt River Project) and APS lead contractor onboarding
Focus on cooling-dominant climate heat pump systems
Low-income customers prioritized in initial pilot phase
Electric panel upgrades essential for whole-home electrification
Statewide expansion planned based on pilot results

md.name: Maryland
md.tagline: Save thousands on energy-efficient home upgrades through MEA and utility programs
notes: Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) coordinates state and federal programs
BGE, Pepco, Delmarva utilities offer stacking heat pump rebates
Income documentation required at application
EmPOWER Maryland provides additional low-income weatherization
Strong contractor network with BPI and HVAC Excellence certifications

fl.name: Florida
fl.tagline: Federal HEAR rebates available while state program development continues
notes: State HEAR program application submitted, pending federal approval
Federal rebates available now for income-qualified households
Duke Energy Florida, FPL, TECO offer limited heat pump rebates
High cooling loads make heat pumps attractive for year-round efficiency
Contact local utilities for current efficiency programs

tx.name: Texas
tx.tagline: Federal rebates and utility programs available while state coordination develops
notes: State program not yet launched - federal HEAR still available
Check with local utility providers (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas)
Federal rebates available for income-qualified households
Deregulated market creates variability in utility rebate availability
